mcq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{Parseval's identity for Fourier cosine transforms applied to two functions } f(x) \text{ and } g(x) \text{ states:}\)
\(\text{Using Parseval's identity for Fourier cosine transforms with } f(x)=e^{-ax} \text{ and } g(x)=e^{-bx}, \text{ evaluate } \int_0^\infty \frac{dx}{(x^2+a^2)(x^2+b^2)}.\)
\(\text{For } a=2, b=3, \text{ the value of } \int_0^\infty \frac{dx}{(x^2+4)(x^2+9)} \text{ using Parseval's identity is:}\)
\(\text{Using Parseval's identity for Fourier sine transforms with } f(x)=e^{-ax} \text{ and } g(x)=e^{-bx}, \text{ what integral would be evaluated?}\)

\(\text{Given } F_c\{e^{-x}\} = \sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}} \frac{1}{1+s^2} \text{ and } F_c\{e^{-2x}\} = \sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}} \frac{2}{4+s^2}, \text{ use Parseval's identity to find } \int_0^\infty \frac{dx}{(x^2+1)^2}.\)

sq.ANSWER:
Upto the stepMarks

\(\text{Identity: } \int_{0}^{\infty} |f(x)|^2 dx = \int_{0}^{\infty} |F_c(s)|^2 ds\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{Take } f(x)=e^{-x}, \text{ then } F_c(s) = \sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}} \frac{1}{1+s^2}\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{LHS: } \int_{0}^{\infty} e^{-2x} dx = \frac{1}{2}\)

(1 Mark)

\(\text{RHS: } \int_{0}^{\infty} \frac{2}{\pi} \frac{1}{(1+s^2)^2} ds\)

(1 Mark)

\(\text{Equate: } \frac{1}{2} = \frac{2}{\pi} \int_{0}^{\infty} \frac{1}{(1+s^2)^2} ds\)

(1 Mark)

\(\text{Hence } \int_{0}^{\infty} \frac{dx}{(x^2+1)^2} = \frac{\pi}{4}.\)

(1 Mark)
sq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{State Parseval's identity for Fourier cosine transform and use it to evaluate } \int_{0}^{\infty} \frac{dx}{(x^2+1)^2}.\)

sq.ANSWER:
Upto the stepMarks

\(\text{Identity: } \int_{0}^{\infty} |f(x)|^2 dx = \int_{0}^{\infty} |F_s(s)|^2 ds\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{Take } f(x)=e^{-x}, \text{ then } F_s(s) = \sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}} \frac{s}{1+s^2}\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{LHS: } \int_{0}^{\infty} e^{-2x} dx = \frac{1}{2}\)

(1 Mark)

\(\text{RHS: } \int_{0}^{\infty} \frac{2}{\pi} \frac{s^2}{(1+s^2)^2} ds\)

(1 Mark)

\(\text{Equate: } \frac{1}{2} = \frac{2}{\pi} \int_{0}^{\infty} \frac{s^2}{(1+s^2)^2} ds\)

(1 Mark)

\(\text{Hence } \int_{0}^{\infty} \frac{x^2}{(x^2+1)^2} dx = \frac{\pi}{4}.\)

(1 Mark)
sq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{State Parseval's identity for Fourier sine transform and use it to evaluate } \int_{0}^{\infty} \frac{x^2}{(x^2+1)^2} dx.\)

lq.ANSWER:
StepMarks
For Fourier cosine transform: \(\int_{0}^{\infty} [f(x)]^2 dx = \int_{0}^{\infty} [F_c(s)]^2 ds\)(3)
For Fourier sine transform: \(\int_{0}^{\infty} [f(x)]^2 dx = \int_{0}^{\infty} [F_s(s)]^2 ds\)(3)
where \(F_c(s) = \mathcal{F}_c\{f(x)\}\) and \(F_s(s) = \mathcal{F}_s\{f(x)\}\)(2)
General form: \(\int_{0}^{\infty} f(x)g(x) dx = \int_{0}^{\infty} F_c(s)G_c(s) ds = \int_{0}^{\infty} F_s(s)G_s(s) ds\)(4)
lq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{State Parseval's identities for Fourier cosine and sine transforms.}\)
